name: Statsdot Analytics
author: statsdot

sections.description:
Statsdot is simple web analytics that works without cookies and without storing personal data. This plugin adds the Statsdot script to your site, so you can see on one screen:

  • Visitors and pageviews, compared with the previous period, and visitors right now
  • Where visitors come from: search engines, social networks, other sites and UTM campaigns
  • Top, entry and exit pages
  • Countries, devices, browsers and operating systems
  • Outbound link clicks and file downloads, counted automatically
  • Goals and conversion rates
  • With WooCommerce: “Add to cart” and “Purchase” events, ready to use as goals
  • Optional AI crawler tracking: which AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot…) read your pages

The script weighs under 2 KB, loads deferred and sets no cookies. Visitors are counted with a hash that changes every day, so nobody can be followed from one day to the next and the IP address is never stored. That is why Statsdot is designed to run without a cookie banner. Whether your site needs a banner also depends on everything else it loads.

The dashboard is available in English, Spanish, German, French, Italian and Portuguese.

How it works

  1. Install and activate this plugin. Activating it loads nothing yet.
  2. In Settings > Statsdot, click “Connect your Statsdot account” (or “Create a free trial account”: 30 days free, no card needed). Statsdot opens in a small window where you log in or sign up and choose the site, or add this one. Connecting turns on tracking.
  3. Visits show up in your Statsdot dashboard a few seconds later.

Tracking stays off until you turn it on. Logged-in administrators are not counted by default, and nothing is loaded in the WordPress admin.

External services

This plugin relies on Statsdot, a third-party analytics service run by the plugin author, to measure the visits of your site.

  • Nothing is sent and no script is loaded until an administrator connects the plugin or turns on “Measure visits with Statsdot” in Settings > Statsdot. It is off after activation.
  • Connecting: when an administrator clicks “Connect your Statsdot account” or “Create a free trial account”, the browser opens https://statsdot.com/connect/wordpress with this site’s domain, the address of the plugin’s settings page and a random one-time code. Statsdot sends back the domain and the id of the chosen site. Logging in and signing up happen on statsdot.com; the plugin never sees the password.
  • Once it is on, on every page of your site seen by a visitor (not in the admin, and not for logged-in administrators unless you change the setting), the browser loads the script https://statsdot.com/js/script.js.
  • The script sends to https://statsdot.com/api/collect, for each page view: the page address (Statsdot keeps the path only, without query string, and removes order numbers such as /checkout/order-received/1234/), the referring page address (Statsdot keeps only its domain), the UTM campaign tags of the landing page and the screen width (to tell mobile, tablet or desktop). For events it also sends the event name and an optional label: clicks on outbound links and file downloads are sent with the link or file address without query string, unless you turn them off in the settings.
  • With every request the browser sends its IP address and user agent. The Statsdot server uses them only in memory to compute a visitor code that changes every day and to recognise bots, and derives the browser and operating system names from the user agent, which it stores. It does not store the IP address or the user agent. The country comes from the request.
  • With WooCommerce, the events “Add to cart” and “Purchase” (with the order total and currency, optional) are sent with no other order or customer data.
  • AI crawler tracking (optional, only when you paste a bot key in the settings): when a request comes from a known crawler (its user agent matches the Statsdot crawler directory), your server sends to https://statsdot.com/api/bots the crawler’s user agent, the requested address and the HTTP status code. Nothing is sent for human visitors.
  • No cookies are set and nothing is stored on the visitor’s device.

Terms of service: https://statsdot.com/terms
Privacy policy: https://statsdot.com/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin from Plugins > Add New, or upload the statsdot-analytics folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate it.
  3. In Settings > Statsdot, click “Connect your Statsdot account” and choose the site. To set it up by hand instead, turn on “Measure visits with Statsdot” and make sure the domain is the one you added in your Statsdot account.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Statsdot account?

Yes. The plugin only adds the script; the statistics are in your dashboard at statsdot.com. Every account starts with a 30-day free trial without a card.

Does it work with caching plugins?

Yes. The script is a normal external script, so page caching does not affect it. If a plugin combines or delays JavaScript, exclude statsdot.com/js/script.js from it.

How do I count sign-ups or contact forms?

Add the attribute data-statsdot-event="Signup" to a button, link or form, or call window.statsdot.track('Signup') from your code. Then add the event as a goal in Statsdot. See https://statsdot.com/guides/events-and-goals

What is sent for WooCommerce purchases?

The event “Purchase”, once per order, with the order total and currency, so Statsdot can show revenue per source, campaign and page (turn it off in Settings > Statsdot). Optionally, and off by default, the order number: Statsdot keeps a keyed hash of it for 7 days so a test or wrong order can be deleted through its API, then forgets it. No products or customer details are sent, and Statsdot removes the order number from the thank-you page address.

Does it slow my site down?

The script is under 2 KB compressed and loads deferred, after the page.
sections.changelog:
1.4.0

  • “Connect your Statsdot account”: log in or sign up in a small window and choose the site, or add this one, without copying anything. Connecting turns on tracking.

1.3.0

  • Tracking is off after activation and loads nothing until you turn it on in Settings > Statsdot. If you update from an earlier version, turn it on there.
  • Fixed saving the settings and the layout of the “Links and downloads” row.

1.2.0

  • Optional scroll depth (adds data-scroll to the script tag).
  • “Purchase” carries the order total and currency, so the dashboard shows revenue per source, channel, campaign and page (optional). The order number can be added, off by default, to delete test or wrong orders for 7 days.

1.1.0

  • AI crawler tracking: with a bot key, see which AI crawlers read your pages.

1.0.0

  • First release: adds the Statsdot script, excludes administrators, optional outbound link and download tracking, WooCommerce “Add to cart” and “Purchase” events.

short_description: Cookieless, privacy-friendly web analytics made in Europe. Visitors, pages, sources and WooCommerce conversions, without cookies or personal data.
